title: SC sets aside Punjab & Haryana HC verdict, restores MCG's rights over 274 acres in Gurugram - India's News.Net
full_text:
New Delhi [India], August 5 (ANI): The Supreme Court on Monday restored the ownership of over 274 acres (436 bighas and 18 biswas) of disputed land in Haiderpur, Gurugram, to the Municipal Corporation Gurugram (MCG), holding that the land is shamlat deh (village common land) and cannot be treated as private property merely because revenue records mention the names of village proprietors.
The Court set aside a 2007 Punjab and Haryana High Court judgment that had recognised private ownership claims over the land.
A Bench of Justice Sanjay Kumar and Justice K. Vinod Chandran held that the land is governed by the Haryana Common Lands (Regulation) Act, 1961, and upheld the mutation dated September 13, 1955, in favour of the then Gram Panchayat, Wazirabad. The Court ruled that the rights of the Gram Panchayat subsequently stood transferred to the Municipal Corporation Gurugram after its constitution.
In its 85-page judgment, the Court observed that land has become the 'new gold', particularly in rapidly expanding urban areas such as Gurugram, making disputes over village common land increasingly contentious. It cautioned that historical village commons cannot lose their legal character merely because the names of proprietors or pattis appear in revenue records.
The dispute concerns 436 bighas and 18 biswas of land situated in Haiderpur, an uninhabited (be chiraag) village adjoining Wazirabad in Gurugram. After the enactment of the Punjab Village Common Lands legislation, the land was mutated in favour of the Gram Panchayat, Wazirabad, in September 1955 pursuant to a government communication issued in March 1954.
The litigation began in 1985 when four residents of Wazirabad filed proceedings under Section 13A of the Haryana Common Lands (Regulation) Act, 1961, claiming to represent the proprietors of different pattis of Haiderpur.
They challenged the 1955 mutation, contending that the land belonged to private proprietors, had never been used for common village purposes and therefore could not vest in the Gram Panchayat. They also alleged that the mutation had been sanctioned without issuing notice to the proprietors.
The matter underwent several rounds before the revenue authorities. In 1990, the Assistant Collector partly accepted the proprietors' claim. After the matter was remanded, the Assistant Collector again held substantially in their favour, declaring that except for a small portion comprising a pond and a village pathway, the remaining land belonged to the proprietors. The Collector upheld that decision in 1998.
However, in 2005, the Commissioner, Gurgaon Division, reversed the findings of the revenue authorities and restored the 1955 mutation in favour of the Gram Panchayat. The Punjab and Haryana High Court, in 2007, set aside the Commissioner's order, describing it as a non-speaking order, and restored the decisions of the Assistant Collector and Collector. The Supreme Court stayed the operation of the High Court judgment in January 2008.
During the hearing before the apex court, historical revenue records, including Jamabandis dating back to 1877, 1885 and 1905, were produced. The Court noted that these documents had not been placed before either the statutory authorities or the High Court. It also recorded that despite the Commissioner's interim stay order passed in April 1998, as many as 272 sale deeds were executed and corresponding mutations were sanctioned in favour of various private individuals and companies during the pendency of the dispute.
After examining the historical revenue records, the Sharat Wajib-ul-Arz and the statutory framework governing village common lands, the Supreme Court held that the records consistently described the disputed land as shamlat deh and not shamlat patti. The Bench observed that although the proprietors had a right to seek partition of the common land in accordance with their respective shares, no such partition had taken place before January 26, 1950.
As a result, the land retained its character as village common land and vested in the Gram Panchayat under Section 2(g)(1) of the Haryana Common Lands (Regulation) Act, 1961.
The Court further held that where revenue records describe land as shamlat deh, and there is no evidence that it had been partitioned or brought under the separate cultivating possession of individual proprietors before January 26, 1950, it is unnecessary to independently establish that the land was being used for common village purposes.
According to the Bench, the High Court and the revenue authorities failed to attach due importance to the Sharat Wajib-ul-Arz and the historical revenue records, which conclusively established the nature of the land.
Holding that the plaintiffs had failed to establish any legal basis for setting aside the 1955 mutation, the Supreme Court allowed the appeals, quashed the Punjab and Haryana High Court's judgment and restored the mutation in favour of the Gram Panchayat, Wazirabad.
The Court clarified that the benefit of the mutation would now enure to the Municipal Corporation Gurugram, which has succeeded to the rights of the Gram Panchayat. (ANI)

title: Russia’s ‘Black Widow’ Scam Leaves Soldiers’ Families Fighting for War Compensation - english.punjabkesari.com
full_text:
Russia Ukraine war: As Russia’s military casualties continue to mount in the war in Ukraine, a disturbing trend has emerged that is leaving grieving families without the financial support intended for them. Across the country, allegations are growing that some women are entering into rushed marriages with soldiers shortly before they are deployed—or even while they are critically injured—to gain access to generous state compensation paid after a serviceman’s death.
The practice, now widely referred to as the “black widow scam,” has triggered public anger, court disputes and calls for legal reform. Several reported cases suggest that legal loopholes surrounding wartime marriages have enabled strangers, rather than close relatives, to become the primary beneficiaries of government death payments, prompting renewed scrutiny of Russia’s compensation system.
Russia’s Fast-Track Marriages Under Scrutiny
The controversy stems from changes introduced in 2022, when Russia simplified marriage procedures for military personnel joining the armed forces. Waiting periods were removed to allow soldiers to marry quickly before deployment, a measure that was publicly promoted as a way to support military families during wartime.
However, critics argue that the same rules have also created opportunities for exploitation. Under current Russian law, a soldier’s legal spouse is generally recognised as the primary next of kin and becomes eligible for state compensation if the serviceman dies in combat. Those payments reportedly begin at around five million rubles.
Families Say They Were Left With Nothing
One of the cases highlighted by CNN involved Maria from St. Petersburg, who discovered after her father Yury’s death that he had secretly married a woman 22 years younger just two days before leaving for the front. Because of that marriage, the new wife became the legal beneficiary of his compensation.
Maria later found that her father’s apartment had already been sold, leaving her without either the family home or access to the government payout. She has maintained that she had never met or even heard of the woman before her father’s death.
Hospitals and Courts See Similar Cases
Reports suggest the alleged scheme extends beyond isolated incidents. In one widely discussed case, a military hospital nurse was dismissed after being accused of marrying several wounded soldiers under her care shortly before they died from their injuries.
Another controversy emerged in Tomsk, where a real estate agent publicly suggested that marrying a deployed soldier could provide enough compensation to purchase an inexpensive apartment. The remarks triggered widespread condemnation, and those involved were later sentenced to community service and ordered to issue public apologies.
Legal Challenges Grow
Not every disputed marriage has resulted in compensation being awarded. In Ryazan, soldier Georgy Kostyrko married Angelina Varyukhina only days after meeting her online. Although he later sought a divorce, he was killed before the proceedings were completed.
His mother challenged Varyukhina’s claim in court, arguing that the marriage should not entitle her to survivor benefits. The court ultimately revoked her next-of-kin status, a rare ruling that has intensified calls for stronger legal safeguards to ensure compensation reaches genuine family members rather than opportunistic claimants.

title: Sheikh Hasina Chokes Up in First Public Address Since Exile, Defends Her Legacy - english.punjabkesari.com
full_text:
Sheikh Hasina Breaks Silence: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina made her first public appearance in nearly two years on Wednesday, delivering an emotional virtual address in which she said she had watched her country “suffer” since being forced into exile following the August 2024 uprising. Speaking remotely at an event organised by the Foreign Correspondents Club of South Asia, the 78-year-old Awami League chief repeatedly broke down while recalling Bangladesh’s Liberation War, her assassinated family members and the political turmoil that followed her removal from power.
Rejecting allegations against her, Hasina defended her government’s handling of the 2024 protests, describing them as a politically driven campaign rather than a peaceful student movement. She also vowed not to be intimidated by legal proceedings against her.
Sheikh Hasina Says Bangladesh Has Drifted From Liberation Ideals
Addressing the gathering from exile in India, Hasina said the Bangladesh she sees today is far removed from the nation envisioned during the 1971 Liberation War.
“For the last two years, I watched my beloved Bangladesh suffer. This is not the Bangladesh we built; this is not the Bangladesh for which three million people sacrificed their lives in 1971,” she said, her voice breaking as she remembered those who died during the war and members of her own family.
Defends Government’s Response To 2024 Protests
Hasina strongly rejected the narrative surrounding the July-August 2024 protests that ultimately ended her 15-year rule.
She claimed her government initially attempted to resolve the unrest through dialogue, legal measures and patience, but alleged that organised political groups transformed genuine student demands into a broader movement aimed solely at removing her from office.
According to Hasina, what began as calls for reform eventually became a coordinated political campaign that turned violent.
Rejects Death Sentence, Calls Trial Politically Motivated
The former prime minister dismissed the death sentence handed to her in absentia by a special tribunal last year, which convicted her of crimes against humanity over the deadly crackdown on anti-government demonstrations.
Calling the proceedings “illegal, unconstitutional and politically motivated,” Hasina said neither the verdict nor the criminal cases filed against her would deter her.
“A death sentence, false cases and staged trials cannot frighten me,” she said.
Exile In India And Political Uncertainty
Hasina has been living in India since August 5, 2024, after fleeing Bangladesh as protesters advanced toward her official residence.
In her written remarks, she said she had only “30 to 40 minutes” to leave and insisted she never intended to go into exile.
“I did not even know I was leaving the country,” she said, adding that she had planned to travel to her ancestral home in Tungipara instead.
Bangladesh Government Maintains Tough Position
The current Bangladesh government, led by the Bangladesh Nationalist Party under Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, has maintained that Hasina will face legal action if she returns.
Law Minister M. Asaduzzaman stated in late July that the former prime minister would likely be arrested immediately upon her arrival in Bangladesh before being allowed to surrender before a court.
Meanwhile, Hasina’s Awami League remains banned from political activity, and she continues to face multiple criminal cases linked to the 2024 unrest.
International Scrutiny
The violence surrounding the 2024 anti-government protests drew widespread international attention. According to United Nations estimates, around 1,400 people were killed during the unrest, making it one of the deadliest periods in Bangladesh’s recent political history.
Hasina’s address marks her most significant public intervention since her ouster, as political divisions in Bangladesh continue over accountability, democratic legitimacy and the country’s future direction.

title: Authorities Warn Private Schools Over Summer Vacation Violations - TechJuice
full_text:
The Lahore Education Authority has warned all private educational institutions across the city that strict legal action will follow any violation of the summer vacation schedule, which is to remain in effect until August 22, 2026.
According to the authority, private schools are required to ensure full compliance with the directive. Institutions found in violation will face action under the law, which may include suspension or cancellation of school registration along with heavy fines.
The authority has also made clear that individuals responsible for such violations will face further legal and administrative action, and the district administration may be approached with a recommendation to seal any non-compliant school if required.
The current vacation schedule stems from a broader Punjab government decision announced in May, under which all public and private schools across the province were closed starting Friday, May 22, 2026, with the closure applying to every level, from primary to higher secondary institutions.
The extended break was announced in response to heatwave warnings from the PDMA and PMD, which had forecast above-normal temperatures across the province throughout May, June and July, while also aligning the summer vacation with the Eid-ul-Adha holidays.
For 2026, the provincial government ruled out exemptions that some elite private institutions had previously sought to continue O and A-Level preparation during the break, stating that institutions found operating after May 22 would face regulatory action, including possible suspension of registration.
The length of the closure has faced pushback from private school bodies. Four of the main private school associations rejected the schedule, describing the roughly 90-day closure as harmful to academic activity, and said they would challenge the decision before the Lahore High Court, including its Rawalpindi, Multan and Bahawalpur benches.
The All Pakistan Private Schools and Colleges Association said long vacations reduce student interest in studies while increasing screen time and non-academic activities, warning that extended breaks could further affect the education of children already out of school.
Despite the objections, enforcement has continued. Show-cause notices have previously been issued to private schools that reopened ahead of the approved date, following surprise inspections that found institutions operating during the break in breach of the Punjab Private Educational Institutions Act.

full_text:
ਮੁਹਾਲੀ: ਪੰਜਾਬ ਸਰਕਾਰ ਨੇ ਸਿੱਖਿਆ, ਰੁਜ਼ਗਾਰ, ਪ੍ਰਸ਼ਾਸਨ ਅਤੇ ਵਾਤਾਵਰਣ ਦੇ ਖੇਤਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੱਡੇ ਸੁਧਾਰਾਂ ਵੱਲ ਕਦਮ ਚੁੱਕਦਿਆਂ ਕੈਬਨਿਟ ਮੀਟਿੰਗ ਵਿੱਚ ਕਈ ਮਹੱਤਵਪੂਰਨ ਫੈਸਲਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਮਨਜ਼ੂਰੀ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਹੈ। ਮੁੱਖ ਮੰਤਰੀ ਦੀ ਅਗਵਾਈ ਹੇਠ ਹੋਈ ਕੈਬਨਿਟ ਬੈਠਕ ਵਿੱਚ ਤਿੰਨ ਨਵੀਆਂ ਡਿਜੀਟਲ ਓਪਨ ਯੂਨੀਵਰਸਿਟੀਆਂ ਸਥਾਪਤ ਕਰਨ, ਪ੍ਰਾਈਵੇਟ ਸਕੂਲਾਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਫੀਸਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਨਿਯਮਤ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਫੀਸ ਰੈਗੂਲੇਸ਼ਨ ਸੋਧ ਬਿੱਲ 2026 ਨੂੰ ਮਨਜ਼ੂਰੀ ਦੇਣ ਅਤੇ ਠੇਕਾ ਕਰਮਚਾਰੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਰਾਹਤ ਦੇਣ ਸਮੇਤ ਕਈ ਅਹਿਮ ਫੈਸਲੇ ਲਏ ਗਏ।
ਕੈਬਨਿਟ ਦੇ ਫੈਸਲਿਆਂ ਅਨੁਸਾਰ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਵਿੱਚ ਤਿੰਨ ਡਿਜੀਟਲ ਓਪਨ ਯੂਨੀਵਰਸਿਟੀਆਂ ਸਥਾਪਤ ਕੀਤੀਆਂ ਜਾਣਗੀਆਂ, ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦਾ ਉਦੇਸ਼ ਵਿਦਿਆਰਥੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਆਧੁਨਿਕ ਤਕਨਾਲੋਜੀ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਉੱਚ ਸਿੱਖਿਆ ਦੀ ਸਹੂਲਤ ਪ੍ਰਦਾਨ ਕਰਨਾ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਯੂਨੀਵਰਸਿਟੀਆਂ ਆਨਲਾਈਨ ਅਤੇ ਡਿਜੀਟਲ ਪਲੇਟਫਾਰਮਾਂ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਪੜ੍ਹਾਈ ਦੀ ਸਹੂਲਤ ਦੇਣਗੀਆਂ, ਜਿਸ ਨਾਲ ਪਿੰਡਾਂ, ਦੂਰ-ਦਰਾਜ਼ ਖੇਤਰਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਨੌਕਰੀਪੇਸ਼ਾ ਵਿਦਿਆਰਥੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਵੀ ਉੱਚ ਸਿੱਖਿਆ ਹਾਸਲ ਕਰਨ ਦਾ ਮੌਕਾ ਮਿਲੇਗਾ। ਸਰਕਾਰ ਦਾ ਮੰਨਣਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਇਹ ਕਦਮ ਸੂਬੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਡਿਜੀਟਲ ਸਿੱਖਿਆ ਨੂੰ ਨਵੀਂ ਦਿਸ਼ਾ ਦੇਵੇਗਾ।
ਸਰਕਾਰ ਨੇ ਪ੍ਰਾਈਵੇਟ ਸਕੂਲਾਂ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਫੀਸਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਕੀਤੇ ਜਾਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਵਾਧੇ ਨੂੰ ਨਿਯੰਤਰਿਤ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਫੀਸ ਰੈਗੂਲੇਸ਼ਨ (ਸੋਧ) ਬਿੱਲ-2026 ਨੂੰ ਵੀ ਮਨਜ਼ੂਰੀ ਦੇ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਹੈ। ਇਸ ਬਿੱਲ ਨੂੰ ਆਰਡੀਨੈਂਸ ਦੇ ਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਲਾਗੂ ਕਰਨ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਸਤਾਵ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ, ਤਾਂ ਜੋ ਮਾਪਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਬੇਲੋੜੇ ਫੀਸ ਵਾਧੇ ਤੋਂ ਰਾਹਤ ਮਿਲ ਸਕੇ। ਸਰਕਾਰ ਦਾ ਕਹਿਣਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਇਸ ਕਾਨੂੰਨ ਨਾਲ ਪ੍ਰਾਈਵੇਟ ਸਕੂਲਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਫੀਸਾਂ ਦੀ ਪਾਰਦਰਸ਼ੀ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਆਂਪੂਰਨ ਵਿਵਸਥਾ ਯਕੀਨੀ ਬਣਾਈ ਜਾਵੇਗੀ।
ਕੈਬਨਿਟ ਨੇ ਠੇਕਾ ਆਧਾਰ ‘ਤੇ ਕੰਮ ਕਰ ਰਹੇ ਕਰਮਚਾਰੀਆਂ ਲਈ ਵੀ ਰਾਹਤ ਭਰੇ ਫੈਸਲਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਮਨਜ਼ੂਰੀ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਹੈ। ਹਾਲਾਂਕਿ ਸਰਕਾਰ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਇਸ ਸਬੰਧੀ ਵਿਸਥਾਰਪੂਰਵਕ ਜਾਣਕਾਰੀ ਬਾਅਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਜਾਰੀ ਕੀਤੀ ਜਾਵੇਗੀ, ਪਰ ਉਮੀਦ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਇਸ ਨਾਲ ਹਜ਼ਾਰਾਂ ਕਰਮਚਾਰੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਲਾਭ ਮਿਲੇਗਾ ਅਤੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਲੰਬੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਤੋਂ ਚੱਲ ਰਹੀਆਂ ਮੰਗਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਕੁਝ ਹੱਦ ਤੱਕ ਪੂਰਾ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾ ਸਕੇਗਾ।

ਚੰਡੀਗੜ੍ਹ, 5 ਅਗਸਤ 2026- ਪੰਜਾਬ ਵਿਧਾਨ ਸਭਾ ਵਿਖੇ ਮੁੱਖ ਮੰਤਰੀ ਭਗਵੰਤ ਸਿੰਘ ਮਾਨ ਦੀ ਅਗਵਾਈ ਹੇਠ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਕੈਬਨਿਟ ਦੀ ਇੱਕ ਅਹਿਮ ਮੀਟਿੰਗ ਹੋਈ, ਜਿਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਸੂਬੇ ਦੀ ਤਰੱਕੀ, ਨੌਜਵਾਨਾਂ, ਮੁਲਾਜ਼ਮਾਂ, ਸਿੱਖਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਵਾਤਾਵਰਣ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜੇ ਕਈ ਮਹੱਤਵਪੂਰਨ ਤੇ ਇਤਿਹਾਸਕ ਫੈਸਲਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਮਨਜ਼ੂਰੀ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਗਈ। ਮੀਟਿੰਗ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਵਿੱਤ ਮੰਤਰੀ ਹਰਪਾਲ ਸਿੰਘ ਚੀਮਾ ਨੇ ਪ੍ਰੈੱਸ ਕਾਨਫਰੰਸ ਦੌਰਾਨ ਕੈਬਨਿਟ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਲਏ ਗਏ ਫੈਸਲਿਆਂ ਬਾਰੇ ਵਿਸਥਾਰਪੂਰਵਕ ਜਾਣਕਾਰੀ ਸਾਂਝੀ ਕੀਤੀ
ਵਿੱਤ ਮੰਤਰੀ ਹਰਪਾਲ ਸਿੰਘ ਚੀਮਾ ਨੇ ਦੱਸਿਆ ਕਿ ਨਿੱਜੀ ਸਕੂਲਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਬੇਲੋੜੀ ਅਤੇ ਗੈਰ-ਵਾਜਬ ਫੀਸਾਂ ਦੇ ਵਾਧੇ ਨੂੰ ਰੋਕਣ ਲਈ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਲਿਆਂਦੇ ਗਏ ਆਰਡੀਨੈਂਸ (ਪੰਜਾਬ ਰੈਗੂਲੇਸ਼ਨ ਆਫ਼ ਪੀਸ ਆਫ਼ ਅਨ-ਏਡਿਡ ਐਜੂਕੇਸ਼ਨ) ਨੂੰ ਹੁਣ ਬਿੱਲ ਦੇ ਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਤਬਦੀਲ ਕਰਨ ਦੀ ਮਨਜ਼ੂਰੀ ਦੇ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਗਈ ਹੈ। ਵਿਧਾਨ ਸਭਾ ਵਿੱਚ ਪਾਸ ਹੋਣ ਅਤੇ ਰਾਜਪਾਲ ਦੀ ਪ੍ਰਵਾਨਗੀ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਇਹ ਪੂਰੀ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਕਾਨੂੰਨ ਬਣ ਜਾਵੇਗਾ।
ਇਸ ਕਾਨੂੰਨ ਤਹਿਤ ਸਕੂਲਾਂ ਦੀ ਸਾਲਾਨਾ ਫੀਸ ਵਾਧੇ ਦੀ ਉੱਚਤਮ ਸੀਮਾ 5 ਫੀਸਦੀ ਤੈਅ ਕੀਤੀ ਗਈ ਹੈ। ਜੇਕਰ ਕੋਈ ਸਕੂਲ 5 ਫੀਸਦੀ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਧ ਫੀਸ ਵਧਾਉਣਾ ਚਾਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਤਾਂ ਉਸ ਲਈ ਰੈਗੂਲੇਟਰੀ ਬਾਡੀ ਦਾ ਗਠਨ ਕੀਤਾ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ। ਇਸ ਤੋਂ ਇਲਾਵਾ ਸਕੂਲਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਫੋਰੈਂਸਿਕ/ਆਡਿਟ ਕਰਵਾਉਣ ਦਾ ਵੀ ਵਿਸ਼ੇਸ਼ ਪ੍ਰਬੰਧ ਕੀਤਾ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ।
ਆਊਟਸੋਰਸ ਤੇ ਕੰਟਰੈਕਟ ਕਾਮਿਆਂ ਲਈ ਇਤਿਹਾਸਕ 'ਮਨੀ ਬਿੱਲ'
ਪੰਜਾਬ ਵਿੱਚ ਪਿਛਲੀਆਂ ਸਰਕਾਰਾਂ ਸਮੇਂ ਠੇਕੇਦਾਰਾਂ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਆਊਟਸੋਰਸ 'ਤੇ ਰੱਖੇ ਗਏ ਕਾਮਿਆਂ ਲਈ ਕੈਬਨਿਟ ਨੇ ਇਤਿਹਾਸਕ ਫੈਸਲਾ ਲਿਆ ਹੈ। ਸਰਕਾਰ ਆਊਟਸੋਰਸਿੰਗ 'ਤੇ ਕੰਮ ਕਰਦੇ ਕਾਮਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਸਿੱਧੇ ਤੌਰ 'ਤੇ ਸਰਕਾਰ ਦੇ ਅਧੀਨ ਕੰਟਰੈਕਟ 'ਤੇ ਲਿਆਉਣ ਲਈ ਇੱਕ ਵਿਸ਼ੇਸ਼ ਮਨੀ ਬਿੱਲ (Money Bill) ਲੈ ਕੇ ਆ ਰਹੀ ਹੈ। ਵਿੱਤ ਮੰਤਰੀ ਨੇ ਸਪੱਸ਼ਟ ਕੀਤਾ ਕਿ ਮਨੀ ਬਿੱਲ ਹੋਣ ਕਰਕੇ ਇਸ ਨੂੰ ਵਿਧਾਨ ਸਭਾ ਵਿੱਚ ਪੇਸ਼ ਕਰਨ ਤੋਂ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਰਾਜਪਾਲ ਦੀ ਪੂਰਵ-ਪ੍ਰਵਾਨਗੀ (Prior Approval) ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ, ਜਿਸ ਲਈ ਪ੍ਰਸਤਾਵ ਭੇਜ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ। ਪ੍ਰਵਾਨਗੀ ਮਿਲਦਿਆਂ ਹੀ ਇਸ ਨੂੰ ਵਿਧਾਨ ਸਭਾ ਦੇ ਮੇਜ਼ 'ਤੇ ਰੱਖ ਕੇ ਪਾਸ ਕਰਵਾਇਆ ਜਾਵੇਗਾ।
3 ਨਵੀਆਂ ਡਿਜੀਟਲ ਓਪਨ ਯੂਨੀਵਰਸਿਟੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਮਨਜ਼ੂਰੀ
ਪੰਜਾਬ ਪ੍ਰਾਈਵੇਟ ਡਿਜੀਟਲ ਓਪਨ ਯੂਨੀਵਰਸਿਟੀ ਪਾਲਿਸੀ ਤਹਿਤ ਸੂਬੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਅਤੀ-ਆਧੁਨਿਕ ਡਿਜੀਟਲ ਸਿੱਖਿਆ ਨੂੰ ਉਤਸ਼ਾਹਿਤ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਤਿੰਨ ਨਵੀਆਂ ਯੂਨੀਵਰਸਿਟੀਆਂ ਸਥਾਪਤ ਕਰਨ ਦਾ ਫੈਸਲਾ ਕੀਤਾ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ.. ਹੁਸ਼ਿਆਰਪੁਰ-ਚੰਡੀਗੜ੍ਹ ਰੋਡ 'ਤੇ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੀ ਪਹਿਲੀ ਕਲਾਊਡ ਯੂਨੀਵਰਸਿਟੀ ਬਣੇਗੀ, ਜਿੱਥੇ ਬੱਚਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਅਤੀ-ਆਧੁਨਿਕ ਡਿਜੀਟਲ ਤਰੀਕਿਆਂ ਨਾਲ ਪੜ੍ਹਾਈ ਕਰਵਾਈ ਜਾਵੇਗੀ। ਐੱਮ.ਐੱਸ ਡਿਜੀਟਲ ਯੂਨੀਵਰਸਿਟੀ (ਪਟਿਆਲਾ)/ ਬਲਰਾਜ ਸਿੰਗਲਾ ਐਜੂਕੇਸ਼ਨ ਸੋਸਾਇਟੀ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਪਟਿਆਲਾ ਦੇ ਪਿੰਡ ਫਤਿਹਪੁਰ ਵਿਖੇ ਸਥਾਪਤ ਕੀਤੀ ਜਾਵੇਗੀ। ਦੁਨੀਆ ਭਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਪ੍ਰਸਿੱਧ ਸਿੱਖਿਆ ਬ੍ਰਾਂਡ 'ਫਿਜ਼ਿਕਸ ਵਾਲਾ' (Physics Wallah) ਵੱਲੋਂ ਪਟਿਆਲਾ ਦੇ ਪਿੰਡ ਅਨੰਦਪੁਰ ਕੇਸ਼ਵ ਵਿਖੇ ਡਿਜੀਟਲ ਯੂਨੀਵਰਸਿਟੀ ਖੋਲ੍ਹੀ ਜਾਵੇਗੀ।
ਵਾਤਾਵਰਣ ਦੀ ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਲਈ 'ਪੰਜਾਬ ਪ੍ਰੋਟੈਕਸ਼ਨ ਆਫ਼ ਟ੍ਰੀਜ਼ ਬਿੱਲ'
ਗਲੋਬਲ ਵਾਰਮਿੰਗ ਅਤੇ ਜਲਵਾਯੂ ਪਰਿਵਰਤਨ (ਕਲਾਈਮੇਟ ਚੇਂਜ) ਦੇ ਗੰਭੀਰ ਮੁੱਦੇ ਨੂੰ ਧਿਆਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਰੱਖਦਿਆਂ 'ਪੰਜਾਬ ਪ੍ਰੋਟੈਕਸ਼ਨ ਆਫ਼ ਟ੍ਰੀਜ਼ ਬਿੱਲ' ਨੂੰ ਮਨਜ਼ੂਰੀ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਗਈ ਹੈ। ਨਵੇਂ ਨਿਯਮਾਂ ਅਨੁਸਾਰ ਜੇਕਰ ਕੋਈ ਵਿਅਕਤੀ ਇੱਕ ਰੁੱਖ ਵੱਢੇਗਾ, ਤਾਂ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ 10 ਨਵੇਂ ਪੌਦੇ ਲਗਾਉਣੇ ਪੈਣਗੇ। ਕਾਨੂੰਨ ਦੀ ਉਲੰਘਣਾ ਕਰਨ 'ਤੇ ਪਹਿਲੀ ਵਾਰ 10,000 ਰੁਪਏ ਪ੍ਰਤੀ ਰੁੱਖ ਜੁਰਮਾਨਾ ਹੋਵੇਗਾ। ਦੂਜੀ ਵਾਰ ਉਲੰਘਣਾ ਕਰਨ 'ਤੇ 35,000 ਰੁਪਏ ਜੁਰਮਾਨਾ ਲਗਾਇਆ ਜਾਵੇਗਾ। ਤੀਜੀ ਵਾਰ ਉਲੰਘਣਾ ਕਰਨ 'ਤੇ 50,000 ਰੁਪਏ ਤੱਕ ਦਾ ਭਾਰੀ ਜੁਰਮਾਨਾ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾਵੇਗਾ।
ਪੇਂਡੂ ਵਿਕਾਸ, ਪੰਚਾਇਤ ਅਤੇ ਪਸ਼ੂ ਪਾਲਣ ਵਿਭਾਗ ਦੇ 582 ਵੈਟਰਨਰੀ ਸਬ-ਸੈਂਟਰਾਂ ਦੇ ਪ੍ਰੋਵਾਈਡਰਾਂ, 449 ਵੈਟਰਨਰੀ ਫਾਰਮਾਸਿਸਟਾਂ ਅਤੇ 552 ਸਫ਼ਾਈ ਸੇਵਕਾਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਸੇਵਾਵਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ 1 ਅਪ੍ਰੈਲ 2026 ਤੋਂ 31 ਮਾਰਚ 2027 ਤੱਕ ਦਾ ਵਾਧਾ ਕੀਤਾ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ। ਪੰਜਾਬ ਲੋਕ ਨਿਰਮਾਣ ਵਿਭਾਗ (PWD) ਵਿੱਚ ਸਿਵਲ ਅਸਾਮੀਆਂ 'ਤੇ ਸਿੱਧੇ ਤੌਰ 'ਤੇ ਨਵੀਂ ਭਰਤੀ ਕਰਨ ਨੂੰ ਕੈਬਨਿਟ ਨੇ ਹਰੀ ਝੰਡੀ ਦੇ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਹੈ। ਵਿੱਤ ਮੰਤਰੀ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ ਇਹ ਸਾਰੇ ਫੈਸਲੇ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੇ ਵਿਕਾਸ, ਹਰਿਆਵਲ ਅਤੇ ਨੌਜਵਾਨਾਂ ਦੇ ਸੁਨਹਿਰੀ ਭਵਿੱਖ ਲਈ ਮੀਲ ਦਾ ਪੱਥਰ ਸਾਬਤ ਹੋਣਗੇ।
